title: Dancing and drumming, and getting an MGM job through dancing
summary: Drummers such as Buddy Rich, Louie Bellson and Jo Jones danced; Lee says dancing got him an MGM job on Strike Up the Band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You danced before you played drums, right?
Well ... not really.
Or did you? You played drums before you danced? Do you feel there's a relation?
Oh yeah.
Between dancing and the drum playing?
Yeah, that's why it was so easy to pick up, you know. And Buddy Rich does the same thing, you know.
Well, Louie Bellson was a tap dancer.
Right, right.
Buddy Rich was a tap dancer.
Right.
Cal Tjader was a tap dancer.
Right.
And who else? There's 3 or 4 others, and I've heard an awful lot of drummers say that ...
Yeah, and Jo Jones danced, you know.
I don't believe I remember that.
Yeah ... but Jo danced. He'd get up in a minute and challenge you. And the recent drummers, I guess, too, in later years -- because they played so much for dancers-- and it is so closely related.
That's another story I'll tell you about -- that's how I got a job at MGM playing drums, because I could dance.
With ...
Do you remember "Strike Up the Band" with Mickey Rooney? That was why I got the job.
Was that your first studio job here?
No, that wasn't my first studio job here, but I think I better try to get to bring you up to that part, okay?
Okay. We'll go back, then.
